title: access-ramp-and-infra-readout-sync
summary: POC sync focusing on onboarding progress, access handoff, and environment readiness. SE walked through latency/throughput benchmarks from earlier runs, discussed KV cache warming and prefix caching, flagged a permissions issue with the service account in staging, and agreed next steps for SSO metadata, KMS access, and a short productionish benchmark next week. Action items and owners captured.
action_items: Priya - Send SSO metadata and SAML contact details by 2026-05-10
Tom - Fix staging service-account IAM rules and confirm via Slack by 2026-05-07
Miguel - Run a 1-hour throughput benchmark with client traffic profile and share sheet by 2026-05-13
Anna - Share pricing pilot worksheet and dedicated capacity options by 2026-05-08
Lee - Schedule follow-up demo for security team the week of 2026-05-11
next_steps: Redwood to re-run a 60min bench with KV cache warm start and provide token-level breakdown
Customer to validate staging IAM and provide SSO metadata
Security deep-dive scheduled pending SSO metadata
Plan for short productionlike run next Wednesday (tentative)
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-06 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Anna Keller (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Lee Tran (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (BlueWave Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (BlueWave Infra), Sarah Lee (BlueWave Security), Jamal Carter (BlueWave Product)

Summary (auto): Quick sync to validate infra readiness and unblock pilot ramp. Some IAM hiccup in staging, otherwise early bench looks promising with warm KV cache.

[00:00] Anna Keller: "Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick roll-call?"
[00:08] Priya Nair: "Priya here, sorry bit later, pulled from another meeting but I'm on. Priya Nair, Head of ML."
[00:13] Tom Reynolds: "Tom - infra, I'll be looking at service accounts and firewall rules."
[00:18] Sarah Lee: "Sarah from security, just listening for the SSO and KMS parts."
[00:23] Miguel Santos: "Miguel, Redwood SE, I'll kick off the bench review in a bit."
[00:28] Anna Keller: "Great. Agenda: quick infra readout, Miguel walks through the results from the overnight run, then we triage the staging IAM issue and outline the week ahead."

[01:02] Miguel Santos: "Alright, so I have the run from 03:00 - it's a mixed traffic profile, 80/20 short prompts to long context. We did two variants: cold start and warm KV cache. Warm cache reduced p99 from about 290ms to 140ms on the 8k sequence tests, and token-per-second throughput improved roughly 1.6x. Those numbers are from our hosted shim but should be representative for Dedicated too once the kernel mapping is right."
[01:35] Jamal Carter: "When you say KV cash, you mean the key-value cache? sometimes the transcript shows K V cash in our sheets."
[01:42] Miguel Santos: "Yes sorry, KV cache - the prefix/KV caching. Warm prefix cache made a big diff on repeated context calls, which matches what we see in the pilot traffic profile."

[02:10] Priya Nair: "That's encouraging. What was the quantization profile you ran? We care about FP16 versus 8-bit dynamic because of quality for clinical note generation."
[02:20] Miguel Santos: "We ran q4f16 and a q8mm baseline. Quality delta was small on rouge/bleu like metrics — anecdotal evals looked fine but we'd recommend running your prompt suite to confirm. Our Optimize team usually suggests trying q4f16 for latency gains while monitoring the eval set."

[03:01] Tom Reynolds: "Quick note - when I tried to pull logs from staging this morning the service account hit permission denied on the gateway. I opened a ticket but wanted to flag it; can't run the infra smoke without that."
[03:12] Lee Tran: "Did you get the role mapping doc?"
[03:15] Tom Reynolds: "I saw it but the SA doesn't have the right iam.roles/impersonate entries. I'll need Redwood to confirm which permissions the service account requires exactly."
[03:25] Anna Keller: "Yeah we'll paste the minimal IAM policy in the shared doc after the call. Miguel, can you list the permissions?"

[03:40] Miguel Santos: "Minimal: compute.networkUser, storage.read, secretmanager.access, iam.serviceAccountUser plus optional KMS.decrypt if you're going to let Redwood-run keys access. We'll put the exact snippet in the Confluence page. Also note, if you're using customer-managed keys (CMKs) you'll need to add the Redwood service principal to the key policy."

[04:20] Sarah Lee: "On KMS - BlueWave uses an internal KMS broker. We need to verify key rotation and make sure Redwood's access is audit logged. Does Redwood support HSM-backed keys or do you require AWS KMS?"
[04:33] Miguel Santos: "We support bringing your own KMS via our private connector; HSM-backed is fine if you can expose the standard interfaces. We'll capture audit logs and provide a log sink for your SIEM."

[05:00] Anna Keller: "Tom, after you fix the IAM we'll want a quick handshake so Miguel can run a short end-to-end bench from your staging account."
[05:08] Tom Reynolds: "Yep, I'll update the ticket and set the assignee. Expect confirmation by tomorrow afternoon."

[05:40] Miguel Santos: "Back to the bench, one more caveat: the big p99 improvement was only visible when the cache warmed with realistic session reuse. For truly cold-start flows - e.g., new docs every request - the gains are smaller. So we recommend a hybrid: prefix caching for repeated patient context and short session-level cache for rapid replies."

[06:20] Priya Nair: "That matches our traffic. Most users will be following threads, so prefix caching could work. Any concerns about stale cache and privacy for PHI?"
[06:31] Miguel Santos: "We isolate caches per-tenant and also have TTL and invalidation hooks. If you need stronger controls we can disable persistent caching for PHI-heavy endpoints or only enable in Dedicated with strict controls."

[07:05] Jamal Carter: "On cost—how big is the tradeoff? If we warm cache aggressively does cost jump?"
[07:12] Anna Keller: "Short answer: warming increases token cost slightly because you're sending warm requests but it reduces per-response compute. Our Optimize team can model the unit economics for your traffic. I'll share the pilot worksheet after the call."

[07:50] Tom Reynolds: "Question on network egress: do you require open outbound to Redwood endpoints or can we route through a NAT?"
[07:58] Miguel Santos: "NAT with TLS outbound is fine. For Private deployments we can also arrange a VPC peering or private link; for Hosted API simple outbound allowed to our managed endpoints will suffice."

[08:30] Sarah Lee: "SSO: we plan to use Okta. Priya, can you share the SAML metadata? We need to provision the Rails user groups for access. Redwood - do you support SCIM for user provisioning?"
[08:45] Anna Keller: "Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM. We'll need the metadata and a service account with SAML cert. We'll put the SCIM provisioning endpoints in the security pack doc."

[09:20] Priya Nair: "I'll get that by Monday. Also, do you have SOC2 docs? Our procurement asked for SOC and ISO attestation."
[09:28] Lee Tran: "We sent SOC2 Type II last quarter, but I'll re-share the link. Anna, can you put the security pack in the thread?"
[09:34] Anna Keller: "Yep, will repost the SOC2, ISO27001 summary, and the KMS integration guide."

[10:05] Miguel Santos: "I put a public link to the bench spreadsheet in the chat: tinyurl.com/rw-bw-bench. The key tabs: cold-vs-warm, q4f16-vs-q8mm, and token-level breakdown. Note some row labels are truncated in the export, sorry — I see an extra column called 'resp-lat' that should read 'resp-latency' on row 12."
[10:35] Jamal Carter: "I clicked it, seeing the p50/p95/p99 graphs now. For our target SLA of 250ms p95 for short prompts — looks borderline for cold flows."
[10:45] Miguel Santos: "Agree, cold flows will be tighter. Our recommended mitigation: smaller batching window for short prompts and aggressive prefix caching for threads that need the 250ms p95."

[11:20] Tom Reynolds: "Can Redwood run with our on-prem GPU cluster in a private mode? Some of our PHI data can't leave premises for now."
[11:30] Anna Keller: "Yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem deployments and VPC options. We have an on-prem package; there's an onboarding lead who handles appliance and the K8s operator. That is a lift but doable if you decide to go that route."

[12:05] Sarah Lee: "If we did on-prem, what does the patching and security responsibilities look like?"
[12:10] Miguel Santos: "We provide the operator and the runtime images. Customer handles base OS and network; Redwood handles runtime updates, model loading, and can optionally provide patching scripts. We'll add the ops-responsibilities matrix to the doc."

[12:50] Priya Nair: "One slightly weird item: our clinician users saw hallucinations in long-context tests. Did you notice any regression when switching quant profiles?"
[13:03] Miguel Santos: "We did a light eval; q8mm had marginally better factuality in a couple of cases. But it's very prompt dependent — we can run your prompt set across both quant profiles as a next step."

[13:40] Anna Keller: "Ok quick triage: Action on Redwood to run the customer's prompt set across two quant profiles and share results. Miguel will take that."
[13:48] Miguel Santos: "Yes, I'll queue that up once Priya shares the prompt pack."

[14:15] Tom Reynolds: "Back to staging IAM: I put a sample error in the ticket - service account cannot list secrets. I'll make sure the account has secretmanager.access role and then ping here."
[14:24] Lee Tran: "Tom, if you can also add the trace id I can help surface it to our infra team."

[15:00] Anna Keller: "Let's talk timeline: if IAM corrected by tomorrow and Priya shares SSO metadata Monday, we can run the productionlike benchmark next Wednesday and have results by Friday. That keeps the pilot ramp on track for mid-May."
[15:12] Priya Nair: "That timeline works for us. Can you also include a short security walkthrough for our SOC team?"
[15:19] Anna Keller: "Yes, we'll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough. Lee will coordinate."

[16:00] Miguel Santos: "One more item: fallback policy. If a model variant is down we recommend automatic fallback to the slightly higher-latency but higher-availability model. We'll show a sample routing policy in the docs."
[16:12] Jamal Carter: "Good - we want graceful degradation not a hard outage."

[16:45] Sarah Lee: "On audit logs: can Redwood ship per-token traces or just aggregated logs? We need per-request tracing for audit if PHI is involved."
[16:56] Miguel Santos: "We can emit request-level traces to your log sink, but per-customer retention is configurable. We'll need to align on retention policy and redaction rules."

[17:30] Anna Keller: "Alright, let's recap real quick."
[17:35] Anna Keller: "Actions: Tom fixes IAM and confirms; Priya sends SAML metadata and prompt pack; Miguel runs prompt suite and a 60-min bench with warm cache and shares the updated token-level sheet; Anna shares pricing worksheet and security pack; Lee schedules security walkthrough. Next sync after bench results or ad-hoc if IAM not fixed."

[18:10] Priya Nair: "Thanks all, this was helpful. I think the plan is clear. Priya signing off early but I'll watch the thread."
[18:18] Tom Reynolds: "I'll update the ticket after the call."
[18:22] Sarah Lee: "I'll join the security walkthrough next week."
[18:28] Miguel Santos: "I'll start the prompt-suite runs as soon as I have the pack — expecting 24-48 hours to get a clean report."
[18:36] Anna Keller: "Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and the IAM snippet in the shared drive. Chat thread will have the bench link and the SOC pack."

[18:50] (end)

Notes:
- References to shared artifacts: bench sheet (tinyurl.com/rw-bw-bench), security pack link (Confluence: /sec/bluewave), pilot pricing worksheet (Drive: RW-BW-Pricing).
- Minor transcription noise: 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', some truncated column names in the export.
